Checked specifically as instructed. The declaration no longer understates what it leaves unchecked. A residual prose-level observation is recorded as advisory finding F-04.

F-01 MCQ option-length cue. In 6 of the 10 MCQs (items 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8) the key is the longest option, and in items 5, 6 and 7 it is more than twice the length of every distractor. Audit recorded in specs/content/efmp-302/reviews/unit-03/logs-run005/blind-derivation-run005.md before the key was read. A candidate who has not studied the unit can score above chance on those items from length alone. Repair: lengthen the distractors or compress the keys in docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/unit-assessment.mdx items 3-8.

F-02 Bloom labels overstate demand on two MCQs. unit-assessment.mdx MCQ 4 (empathy at excess) and MCQ 7 ("Does everyone understand?") are both labelled (Apply) but each is verbatim recall of a sentence stated in topic-02.mdx and topic-04.mdx respectively, with no new case to transfer to. Of the three Apply-labelled items only MCQ 9 requires application. The front matter blooms_summary claim "three at Apply" therefore overstates demand. The content-spec blueprint range "Remember to Apply" is not breached. Repair: relabel, or supply a fresh mini-case in items 4 and 7.

F-03 Front-matter Bloom description inconsistent with the items. unit-assessment.mdx blooms_summary states "ERQs at Analyze and Evaluate", but ERQ 4 is labelled (Create) and its rubric row is "Design reasoning (Create)". The content-spec blueprint permits "Analyze to Evaluate/Create", so the item is in scope and it is the front-matter description that is inaccurate. Repair: amend blooms_summary to include Create.

F-04 U3-11 grounding is nominal in the prose. coverage/unit-03.md grounds U3-11 in brookfield2017, but docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-05.mdx lines 42-70, the "### The teacher as facilitator and as researcher" section, carries no Brookfield citation. Brookfield's only topic-05 in-prose citation is line 105, inside "### The teacher as life-long learner", which coverage grounds in suarez2022. This is structurally the same defect as the U3-12/suarez2022 case that was repaired by regrounding to no-external-source, and it was not repaired the same way. It does not meet the G3 reference failure condition, because the declaration overstates rather than hides the unverified dependency, which is the safe direction. Since brookfield2017 is unreadable, whether it supports the researcher role cannot be settled here. Repair for the owner: either reground U3-11 as no-external-source, as U3-12 was, or cite Brookfield in that section once the book is obtainable.

F-05 The new depth-gate source-scope cross-check holds, with three named limits. scripts/lib/unit-depth.mjs checkSourceScopeAgreement is wired into the gate, compares both the Supports cell and the ## Unverifiable sources bullets against the coverage matrix in both directions, and 40 depth-gate tests pass at this commit including the two added drift cases (log: logs-run005/depth-gate-crosscheck-tests.log). Limits found by reading the implementation: (a) both loops execute "continue" when the claimed ID set is empty, so a Supports cell or declaration bullet naming no sub-topic ID at all is silently exempt from the check; (b) rows whose Kind is no-external-source are skipped entirely, so that row's own ID claims are never cross-checked against coverage, though in this unit they happen to be correct; (c) the check is set equality on IDs only and never verifies that the prose section for a grounded sub-topic actually cites the key, which is exactly why F-04 survives a passing gate.

F-06 keelson2024 country claim rests on author affiliation. docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-04.mdx and its Further reading both describe the study as "614 university students in Ghana". The bound excerpt at specs/content/efmp-302/sources/texts/keelson2024.md records that 614 and the tertiary setting are confirmed but that Ghana is established by author affiliation to Takoradi Technical University rather than by a stated study location, and recommends the phrasing "a technical university in Ghana". The claim is not false; it is more precise about location than the bound record supports.

F-07 One Goe attribution clause exceeds the bound excerpt. docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-01.mdx:121 states that Goe and colleagues are explicit both that different components suit different purposes, which specs/content/efmp-302/sources/texts/goe2008.md supports directly ("Consider the purpose for the evaluation of teacher effectiveness before deciding on the appropriate measure to employ"), and that "an instrument built for professional development should not be reused for high-stakes appraisal", which is a paraphrase of those recommendations rather than a position the bound text states in that direction. Note also that the excerpt's own "What this settles" section was scoped for the Unit 4 review and was never re-scoped to certify Unit 3 claims. No source outside the bound bundle was consulted to resolve this. Repair: bind a covering excerpt, or mark the direction as an inference in the way topic-01 already marks the Taylor and Thion extension.

F-08 Two authority-trace imprecisions in specs/content/efmp-302/content-spec.md. First, the sub-topic checklist is described as "One row per leaf bullet of course-guide sections 3.1-3.5", but guide section 3.5 has a single leaf bullet naming all five roles and yields three rows (U3-11, U3-12, U3-13): 11 guide leaf bullets against 13 checklist rows. Coverage is expanded rather than reduced, so the direction is safe and no guide content is lost; the self-description is what is inaccurate. Second, content-spec.md:438 traces Unit 3 to "guide CLOs 1, 5", while the guide's on-point outcome for this unit, "Identify and exhibit the characteristics and qualities of an effective teacher", is its second CLO and is claimed only by Unit 1's "CLOs 1-3" range; CLO 1 ("role and responsibilities of teachers") maps only to Topic 3.5. The trace is imprecise rather than contradictory, and every guide leaf bullet for sections 3.1-3.5 is taught.

F-09 "Immediacy" is introduced in docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-04.mdx as a research construct ("verbal immediacy behaviours, which include using pupils' names, inviting questions, and referring to shared classroom experience") and is glossed inline by apposition rather than by a Glossary entry. specs/content/style-guide.md:117-118 asks for a bilingual glossary entry for graduate-level jargon. The inline gloss is adequate for comprehension; the entry would also serve the Urdu pass.

F-10 Narrow-view usability note, not a criterion failure. At 360px the figure scroll regions open at their left edge; for fig-U3-6 the first viewport shows the entry node and the two "no" branch labels but none of the four decision-box texts, so the instructional payload requires horizontal scrolling. The region is keyboard focusable and named, and the alt text carries the full meaning, so the accessibility criterion is met. Evidence: specs/content/efmp-302/reviews/unit-03/render-run005/fig-U3-6-narrow-360-region.png.

F-11 Process, not content. The review-unit skill allows "at most two repair/review cycles per stage per submission" and this is the fifth G3 cycle on EFMP-302 Unit 3. Each cycle followed a genuine change to the bound inputs rather than an unchanged-input retry, so the prohibition on retries seeking a pass is not engaged, but the stated cycle allowance has been exceeded and only the owner can waive it. Recorded so that a passing disposition is not read as having settled that question.
